absent: Frame choice policy and registration effects for ARM MMIO timer, including rate discovery and access selection, are not shown.
Numeric values and layout of PIT hardware constants, mode encodings, latch size and tick rate are absent.
Contracts of clocksource and clockevent registration, broadcast promotion and cpumask handling are not shown.
Jiffies update path, PIT interrupt handling and timekeeping integration are absent.
Expected flag combinations, HZ value, private data use and error precedence for timer framework are not shown.
GIC distributor register offsets, priority encoding, quirk callbacks and controller lock declaration are absent.
V2M probe, bitmap allocation, list lifetime, SPI offset derivation and Graviton detection are not shown.
Parent domain allocation, affinity, acknowledge semantics and MSI descriptor layout are absent.

findings.text: Two platform driver descriptors share one probe routine, one bound via device tree matching and one for ACPI enumeration, both disabling manual bind attributes.

Probe prepares zeroed private and block state when firmware node data exists, otherwise adopts supplied platform data, records the private state, selects a usable timer frame and registers it, failing when no frame qualifies.

Block setup derives control location and extent from the parent resource, then validates each available child for presence, range and uniqueness of its frame identifier before recording its location, extent and both interrupt mappings and marking it usable.
The device tree match uses compatible arm,armv7-timer-mem; driver names are arch-timer-mmio for device tree and gtdt-arm-mmio-timer for ACPI.
A clocksource named pit with rating 110 and 32 bit width exposes a read routine; its init entry registers the source against the PIT tick rate.

PIT timekeeping combines volatile jiffies with a latched hardware countdown into one composite value, preserving prior samples to guarantee forward progress across interrupt latency and documented counter jumps, and reprograms the channel when the latch looks implausible.

All PIT channel accesses and cached sample state serialize on one raw spinlock, with interrupt preserving acquisition in read and disable paths and plain acquisition in mode and event programming paths.

The PIT event object starts periodic capable with shutdown periodic and next event handlers, may gain oneshot capability at init, and shutdown becomes a no operation unless periodic or oneshot state is active.
Two predicates test the event state field for equality with the periodic constant and the oneshot constant respectively.

Disabling reprograms mode, then zero count, then mode again, because some virtual implementations ignore a lone mode write for counting or interrupts and one hypervisor repeats interrupts until mode is rewritten.
Event init optionally enables oneshot support, binds the device to the boot processor, and registers it with tick rate and event limits 15 to 32767.

Oneshot programming adjusts mode alone, periodic programming adjusts mode plus full latch value low byte then high byte, and next event programming writes the requested delta low byte then high byte, each under the shared lock.

The timer framework groups interrupt, mapping and clock descriptors with top level flags, firmware node reference, embedded event object and opaque private storage; interrupt state holds number index name flags handler, mapping state holds pointer name index, clock state holds handle name index rate period.

Framework init honors requested subsets in mapping then clock then interrupt order with partial rollback on failure, defaults an unset event name to the node full name and retains the node; cleanup releases interrupt clock and mapping according to the original request flags.

Interrupt bringup resolves by name when given else by index, rejects a zero mapping, requests the line with caller flags or a timer fallback, and records the number in the embedded event object; teardown frees the recorded line.

Clock bringup acquires by name or index, enables, samples rate and derives period by rounding rate over HZ up, failing on zero rate with disable and release unwind; teardown clears rate then disables and releases.
Mapping bringup requests a named addressed window when a name exists else maps by index and reports failures with node context; teardown unmaps the stored window.
Small helpers obtain the enclosing timer object from its event member and expose the mapped base, interrupt number, clock rate and clock period.
Framework selectors use bit values 1 for base, 2 for clock and 4 for interrupt.
A simplified interrupt request wrapper forwards to the threaded variant with no thread routine while adding a conditional oneshot flag.
Quirk entries carry a description, optional compatible and property selectors, an init callback, plus an identifier and mask for revision comparison.

Firmware quirk scan requires stated compatible and property matches and announces successful init; revision quirk scan ignores firmware selected entries, requires masked identifier equality and likewise announces success.
Interrupt type programming does a locked read modify write of the packed two bit field, clearing for level and setting for edge, skipping the write when already correct and checking the writeback.
Type programming holds a global controller spinlock with interrupt state saved across the read, conditional write and verification.

Shared distributor init forces level low type and uniform priority then clears active and enable for the shared range; private CPU init clears active and enable for the private range then applies uniform priority, both stepping through registers in fixed strides.
A type write whose reread differs reports invalid, which can reflect permission or non secure mode limits rather than a software error, especially for private interrupts.
Redistributor flags use bit 0 for property base flush need, bit 1 for preallocated tables and bit 2 for forced non shareable.
MSI type offset is 8 with base at bit 16 and count in low bits, both masked with 1023; set SPI offset is 64; identifier offset is 4044; valid shared numbers run 32 to 1019 inclusive.
XGene MSI identifier is 0x06000170 and Broadcom NS2 is 0x0000013f; implementation flag 1 requests SPI offset subtraction and flag 2 selects address only encoding.
MSI frame state chains on a list and stores firmware handle, resource, mapped base, start SPI, SPI count, SPI offset, allocation bitmap and implementation flags.
A global spinlock object is declared for version two MSI frame state; guarded fields and acquisition points are not visible in these fragments.

Message composition derives the target from resource start combined with shifted hardware number for address only parts else resource start plus set SPI offset, uses zero payload for address only else hardware number with optional offset subtraction, then splits the address with optional IOMMU translation.

Parent allocation accepts only device tree or irqchip parents, using a three cell rising edge specifier with hardware number minus 32 for the former and a two cell rising edge specifier with raw number for the latter, then forces the parent line to rising edge.
An interrupt chip named GICv2m delegates mask, unmask, acknowledge and affinity to parent handlers and supplies a custom message composer.

Helpers expose chip private data from interrupt state, the MSI descriptor from common state, split of a physical address into high and low message words with optional IOMMU base, and irqchip fwnode detection by operation table identity.
Three header guard macros protect repeated inclusion and one constant defines the GICv2m log prefix.
